served.stem: Sweat glands are distributed across most of the body surface, but they are most densely concentrated in which region?
choices: Spread at the same density over the entire body surface
served.bankWhy: Where sweat glands sit follows what each patch of skin is for. They are densest on the palms, soles, and axillae, which is why nervous sweat shows up in the hands first, and the palms and soles pair that with thick skin and friction ridges for grip. The choice naming palms, soles, and axillae is the concentrated set.

choiceTexts: Spread at the same density over the entire body surface

answer.line: Palms and soles have the densest eccrine sweat glands, and the axillae are where the apocrine glands cluster.

steps: Picture the map. Sweat glands are not spread evenly: density changes several-fold from one region to the next.
Palms and soles lead for eccrine glands, the watery, cooling kind. That is why nervous sweat shows up in your hands first.
Add the axillae for the other kind: apocrine glands cluster there. Together they make the concentrated set.

choices.note: The back is a big surface, so it can shed a lot of sweat in total. Per patch of skin, its glands are sparse.
Eccrine density leads on the palms and soles; apocrine glands cluster in the axillae.

choices.text: Spread at the same density over the entire body surface
choices.note: Density varies several-fold, from hundreds of glands per square centimeter on the palm to far fewer on the trunk.
The lid margin is busy with glands, but they are mostly oil-making. Eyelid skin itself carries few sweat glands.
The red margin of the lips has essentially no sweat glands, one reason lips dry out. It sits at the bottom, not the top.

student.lockIt: Eccrine glands: densest on the palms and soles. Apocrine glands: the axillae.
